data.claim: suitelock.hold races Slots.hold polling every 50 ms; a fresh arrival can win the flock over a waiter that queued earlier, so no order exists
data.falsifier: Four waiters enqueued in order get the lock in a different order, or the refusal lacks a queue position
data.mechanism: Slots.hold sweeps slots with flock LOCK_NB; no ticket or order, the first poller after release wins
data.probe_output: 6 failed against the unfixed code (no ticket queue, refusal lacks pid and queue position); 14 passed with the fix
data.question: Why do gate run ci waiters starve on the host suite lock?

evidence.note: claim CONFIRMED: new queue tests fail on unfixed suitelock.py (6 failed), pass on fixed
r-everything-configurable: stale and grace are knobs [ci].suite_queue_stale_s/grace_s; r-reuse-core: built on Slots+fsio.file_lock

data.text: claim it now at top priority: fix B1fa77a6832 FIFO ci suite lock, then B-gate-run-ci-timeout-under-load, then B-ci-suite-lock-wait-reason-generic

chunk_findings.detail: The added queue design makes each queued waiter hold an flock on its ticket file while waiting and poll every `QUEUE_POLL_S = 0.25` seconds. This violates [r-lock-cycle-selfheal], which states agents never poll-wait or hold while waiting. With multiple CI runs queued for the full-suite lock, every queued agent polls at 4 Hz while holding a lock, which is exactly the pattern the guidance forbids.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:QUEUE_POLL_S

chunk_findings.detail: The new code constructs `SuiteBusy(_holders(directory, limit), time.monotonic() - start, position)` both in the `say(...)` call and in the `raise`. The previous implementation called `SuiteBusy(holders, elapsed)` with only two arguments, and this diff does not update the `SuiteBusy` class. With any non-first waiter, the first time `position != said` it tries to build the exception and gets a `TypeError` instead of a `SuiteBusy` refusal, so the queue wait can crash before timing out or notifying.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:hold

chunk_findings.detail: In `_live`, a `.ticket` is unlinked whenever `fsio.file_lock(path, 0)` can acquire the lock; `age` is checked only on `LockTimeout`. A new or reclaimed `.ticket` is briefly an unlocked file between the rename/open in `_Ticket.__init__`/`__enter__` and the owner actually acquiring the flock. If another waiter scans in that window, it locks and deletes the ticket. The just-created waiter then has no visible directory entry, `_beat` fails on the missing path, and later `_live` scans never include it, so it is treated as last and can be passed by later arrivals.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:_live

chunk_findings.detail: When a waiter times out, `_Ticket.__exit__` renames `self.path` to `.parked` without first calling `_beat`. The parked file keeps the last heartbeat `st_mtime`, not the parking time. If the final `_live()` scan before timeout takes longer than `grace_s`, the just-created parked file is already older than `grace_s`, so the next scanner treats it as expired and deletes it, losing the kept queue place.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:_Ticket.__exit__

chunk_findings.detail: The wait `_until(lambda: _tickets(tmp_path) == 1)` is not a valid barrier here. The first `early` attempt at line 138 has already created a `.ticket` file; for the later retry to keep its place, that ticket must still exist as `*.ticket` after `SuiteBusy`. Therefore `_tickets(tmp_path)` is already `1` before `late = _waiter(...)` is started, so this wait can return immediately before `late` has actually enqueued. The following `_until(lambda: _tickets(tmp_path) == 2)` can then be satisfied by the retained `early` ticket plus `late`'s new ticket before the `early` retry thread is scheduled; the outer holder is released with only `late` ready, making `order == ["early", "late"]` flaky or failing. The condition after starting `late` should require a count that cannot be satisfied by the retained early ticket (or otherwise wait for `late` to have its own ticket), otherwise the test does not exercise the intended “retry keeps place” interleaving deterministically.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suitelock_queue.py:141 test_a_retry_after_giving_up_keeps_its_place

chunk_findings.detail: The new FIFO wait path violates [r-lock-cycle-selfheal] (“agents never poll-wait or hold while waiting”): `QUEUE_POLL_S = 0.25` introduces a 250 ms polling loop, and the module docstring says each waiter “holds an flock on it” while queued. For example, with `max_concurrent_suites=1`, a second suite waits by polling/touching every 250 ms while retaining its ticket flock; a stopped waiter can then hold a live flock without heartbeating, forcing reliance on the added stale-timeout heuristic instead of an event-driven wakeup.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:35 QUEUE_POLL_S

chunk_findings.detail: The test waits only for the `second` waiter’s `say` list to become non-empty (`_until(lambda: bool(said))`) while the holder is still held. Because the first announcement for `second` is the initial enqueue message `"#2 in the queue"`, the wait and the later `any("#2 in the queue" in s for s in said)` are already satisfied before the holder releases. An implementation that never announces the actual change from #2 to #1 (the behavior this test claims to cover) would still pass, so the test does not refute the regression it exists for.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suitelock_queue.py:test_the_place_in_the_queue_is_said_when_it_changes

chunk_findings.detail: The new queue design still defines `QUEUE_POLL_S = 0.25`, and the file docstring says each queued waiter holds an flock on its ticket and periodically touches it while waiting. A run waiting for a full-suite slot therefore polls at 4 Hz while holding a lock for the entire wait, which violates [r-lock-cycle-selfheal]: agents never poll-wait or hold while waiting. The previous LOW finding still holds: nothing in this diff changes the polling interval or removes the per-waiter lock-while-waiting behavior. Concrete scenario: with `[ci].max_concurrent_suites = 1`, start suite A, then suite B; B holds its ticket lock and wakes every 250 ms to heartbeat, exactly the forbidden pattern.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:QUEUE_POLL_S

chunk_findings.detail: The queued waiter still poll-waits while holding a lock. `_Ticket.__enter__` holds a file lock on the ticket for the entire wait, and `hold` loops every `QUEUE_POLL_S` (0.25 s) doing `_live` scans and `time.sleep(QUEUE_POLL_S)`. This is exactly the poll-wait-while-holding pattern forbidden by [r-lock-cycle-selfheal]; the triage note that it is a “process wait, not a lease hold” does not answer it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:hold

chunk_findings.detail: A newly created but not yet flocked ticket is omitted from `live` while age <= `NEW_S`; only an unlocked ticket older than `NEW_S` is unlinked. This lets a later process overtake an earlier one. Interleaving: waiter A enters `_Ticket.__enter__`, where `fsio.file_lock(path, 0)` has created `000...-a.ticket` but A is descheduled between file creation and taking the flock; waiter B then enters with a later timestamp, scans, sees A’s unlocked young ticket and neither appends nor removes it, so `line` is `[B]`, `position == 1`, and B acquires a free slot before A. The arrival order is broken.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:_live

chunk_findings.detail: The `.parked` branch unlinks any parked file older than `grace_s` without first checking whether it is currently locked for reuse. `_Ticket.__enter__` locks `self._parked` before renaming it to `.ticket`, so a scanner can unlink the parked file after that lock is acquired but before the rename. The retry then suppresses the rename `OSError` and the missing-path `_beat`, and enters `hold` with no visible ticket; `position = len(line) + 1` can make it lose the kept place. This is triggered by a retry racing with a scan after its parked ticket exceeds `grace_s`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:_live

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding 1 still holds. The author’s triage (“QUEUE_POLL_S polling is a process wait, not a lease hold”) does not address the poll-wait portion of [r-lock-cycle-selfheal], which forbids agents from poll-waiting or holding while waiting. With multiple CI runs queued behind the full-suite lock, each queued waiter still polls at `QUEUE_POLL_S = 0.25` (4 Hz) while waiting, so the rule violation remains even if this is characterized as a process wait rather than a lease hold.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:QUEUE_POLL_S

chunk_findings.detail: `_until(lambda: _tickets(tmp_path) == 2)` is a race. It waits for the pre-planted stale `frozen` ticket and the new `alive` ticket to coexist, but the alive waiter’s own liveness scan can pass over/unlink the already 600s-old `frozen` ticket as soon as it enters the queue. If that happens before the main thread’s next 20 ms poll, the count goes 1 → 2 → 1 and the predicate is never observed, so the test times out after 10 s even though the suitelock behavior is correct.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suitelock_queue.py:132

chunk_findings.detail: The change still keeps `QUEUE_POLL_S = 0.25` and the module docstring says each queued waiter “holds an flock on it … and touches it as a heartbeat,” so a waiter polls every 250 ms while holding its ticket flock. The triage claim “QUEUE_POLL_S polling is a process wait, not a lease hold” does not answer [r-lock-cycle-selfheal]: the rule forbids poll-waiting (and holding while waiting), not merely lease holds. Concrete failure: with `max_concurrent_suites=1`, a second full-suite run enters the queue, holds its ticket flock, and polls every 0.25 s; if that process is stopped, it still holds the flock without beating until `suite_queue_stale_s` (default 120 s) expires, blocking the queue head.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:35 QUEUE_POLL_S

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier [r-lock-cycle-selfheal] violation still holds. The author’s triage says “QUEUE_POLL_S polling is a process wait, not a lease hold,” but the waiting loop still both poll-waits and holds a lock while waiting: `_Ticket` keeps the ticket `fsio.file_lock` held during `time.sleep(QUEUE_POLL_S)` and `_beat(ticket.path)` every 250 ms. That is exactly the poll/hold-while-waiting pattern the advisory forbids.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:hold (previous finding 1)

chunk_findings.detail: `_parked_for` reuses any matching `.parked` file with no age check, but `_live` treats a `.parked` file older than `grace_s` as dead and removes it. A retry can therefore reclaim an expired park if it runs after the park crosses `grace_s` but before another waiter’s next `_live` scan removes it. That works as a race; it can make a new live waiter already queued lose its place to a retry of a waiter whose reservation is supposed to be dead.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:_parked_for

chunk_findings.detail: Prior finding 2 still holds. The test waits only for `said` to become non-empty while the holder is still held (`_until(lambda: bool(said))`); that first message is the initial enqueue announcement `"#2 in the queue"`. The later check is also only `any("#2 in the queue" in s for s in said)`, so an implementation that never announces the actual change from `#2` to `#1` when the first waiter leaves would still pass. Add an assertion that a `#1` message is emitted after the holder releases.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suitelock_queue.py:test_the_place_in_the_queue_is_said_when_it_changes

chunk_findings.detail: `QUEUE_POLL_S = 0.25` and the new module docstring still define a queue where each waiter holds an flock on its ticket and polls every 0.25 s for the whole wait. That is poll-waiting while holding a lock, which violates [r-lock-cycle-selfheal] (“agents never poll-wait or hold while waiting”). The triage rationale that this is an OS-level Slots/flock wait does not answer the poll-wait/hold part: a run queued behind a long full-suite job still loops at 4 Hz and holds the ticket flock throughout the wait.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:QUEUE_POLL_S

chunk_findings.detail: Still violates [r-lock-cycle-selfheal]. A queued waiter holds an flock on its `ticket.path` for the entire wait, and `hold` loops `time.sleep(QUEUE_POLL_S)` (0.25 s) while holding that lock. The triage that this is an OS-level process wait and cannot form a wait cycle does not answer the rule’s prohibition on poll-waiting or holding while waiting. Concrete case: a CI process behind an occupied full suite polls at 4 Hz while continuing to hold its ticket lock.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:hold

chunk_findings.detail: `_Ticket.__enter__` uses `self._lock.enter_context(fsio.file_lock(self._parked or self.path, 0))` with a nonblocking lock and no retry, while `_live` deliberately takes `fsio.file_lock(path, 0)` on unlocked `.ticket` files (and can race with reclaiming `.parked` files). If a new waiter has created its ticket and is preempted between file creation and taking the flock, another waiter’s `_live` scan can briefly own that flock; when the owner resumes, its `fsio.file_lock(..., 0)` raises `fsio.LockTimeout`, which propagates out of `hold()` instead of queueing or raising `SuiteBusy`. A retry near the `grace_s` boundary has the same race. This is the unaddressed version of the parked-file race: the current code only protects after the claim is already locked, not between `_parked_for` returning the path and `__enter__` acquiring the lock.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:_Ticket.__enter__

chunk_findings.detail: The change still has `QUEUE_POLL_S = 0.25`, and `_Ticket.__enter__` holds the per-waiter ticket flock while `hold` repeatedly runs `_live` and sleeps `QUEUE_POLL_S` until it reaches the head. That is an agent poll-waiting while holding a lock, which violates [r-lock-cycle-selfheal]. The triage that this is an OS-level flock wait and “no lease involved” does not answer the absolute “never poll-wait or hold while waiting” clause: a full-suite CI run still polls at 4 Hz while holding its ticket lock for the entire queued wait.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:hold / QUEUE_POLL_S

chunk_findings.detail: The change still introduces poll-waiting while holding a lock, which violates [r-lock-cycle-selfheal]. `QUEUE_POLL_S = 0.25` and the module docstring specify that each queued waiter “holds an flock on it … and touches it as a heartbeat,” so a waiter sleeps and re-beats its ticket every 250 ms while holding the ticket flock. The triage distinction between “process wait” and “lease hold” does not answer this because the rule forbids both poll-waiting and holding while waiting. Concrete failure: with `max_concurrent_suites=1`, a second full-suite run entering the queue will poll/beat every 0.25 s while holding its ticket lock for up to `[ci].suite_wait_s`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:35, ddflow/services/suitelock.py:8-14

chunk_findings.detail: The previous [r-lock-cycle-selfheal] findings still hold. In `hold`, the loop executes `time.sleep(QUEUE_POLL_S)` and `_beat(ticket.path)` while the `_Ticket` still holds `fsio.file_lock` on that ticket. The triage says the existing `Slots` primitive already polls and is not changed, but this is a new separate ticket-file lock held during the new poll loop. That is exactly poll-waiting while holding a lock, which the rule says agents never do.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:hold

chunk_findings.detail: A legitimate new waiter can be aborted by the scanner. For a new ticket, `_Ticket.__init__` does not create `self.path`; `fsio.file_lock(self.path, 0)` must create and lock the file. The path is visible after creation but before the lock is held. Another waiter's `_live` can see that just-created `.ticket`, and its “created, its owner has not locked it yet” branch calls `fsio.file_lock(path, 0)` itself. If that scanner wins the flock first, the new owner's own `fsio.file_lock` then raises `fsio.LockTimeout`, which `_Ticket.__enter__` does not catch or retry. The new waiter then fails before entering the queue even though it did nothing wrong.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:_live / _Ticket.__enter__

chunk_findings.detail: `test_a_killed_waiter_drops_out_of_the_queue` is inconsistent with the rule asserted later in this same file at line 157-158: a fresh, unlocked `.ticket` file is deliberately counted as live. When the child waiter is killed, its `.ticket` remains fresh (its last heartbeat is milliseconds/seconds old, far below the default 120s stale threshold) and its flock is released by the OS, so `_live` will still include it. The `alive` waiter is behind that live `doomed` ticket and cannot acquire the lock; after `t.join(15)` it is still waiting on its 30s default wait, so `order == ["alive"]` fails. The test therefore fails with the intended semantics.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suitelock_queue.py:115

chunk_findings.detail: Prior finding 4 still holds. `test_the_place_in_the_queue_is_said_when_it_changes` stops waiting as soon as any message is recorded while the holder is still held, and the only queue-position assertion is `any("#2 in the queue" in s for s in said)`. That first message is already the initial `#2 in the queue` announcement, so an implementation that never announces the change from `#2` to `#1` when `first` leaves would still pass. The test does not test its name/intent.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suitelock_queue.py:90

chunk_findings.detail: The change still defines a queue where each waiter holds an flock on its ticket file and polls every 0.25 s (`QUEUE_POLL_S = 0.25`) for the entire wait, and the module docstring describes that behavior. This is poll-waiting while holding a lock, which violates [r-lock-cycle-selfheal] (“agents never poll-wait or hold while waiting”). The intent’s rationale that this is an OS-level flock wait and not a lease does not answer the absolute prohibition: a CI process queued behind a long full-suite job still loops at 4 Hz while holding its ticket flock throughout the wait.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:QUEUE_POLL_S and module docstring

chunk_findings.detail: The pre-existing `SuiteBusy` class was used with exactly two positional arguments (`SuiteBusy(_holders(directory, limit), time.monotonic() - start)`), and this diff does not update it. The new `hold` now calls it with a third positional argument in both `say(str(SuiteBusy(..., position)))` and `raise SuiteBusy(..., position)`. A queued waiter whose `position != said` (e.g. position 2 behind an occupied suite) evaluates the three-argument constructor before the normal timeout path and gets `TypeError`, instead of the intended `SuiteBusy`/queue-position behavior.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:hold

chunk_findings.detail: `_parked_for` returns a parked ticket without atomically claiming it. Two concurrent retries with the same holder `key` can both see and return the same `*.parked` path, then both derive the same `.ticket` path. `_Ticket.__enter__` locks the parked path and renames it while the other retry may already have that path open and be blocking. The second retry then either raises `fsio.LockTimeout` that `hold` does not catch, or renames a newly created parked file over the first retry’s live `.ticket`, leaving that waiter without a visible queue entry.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:_parked_for / _Ticket.__enter__

chunk_findings.detail: This still violates [r-lock-cycle-selfheal]. The hold loop executes `time.sleep(QUEUE_POLL_S)` (0.25 s) while continuing to hold the `_Ticket` flock on `ticket.path`; a worker queued behind a full suite polls at 4 Hz and holds its ticket lock for the entire wait. The triage that an flock-based host semaphore cannot form a task wait cycle does not answer the rule’s absolute “never poll-wait or hold while waiting” clause.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/suitelock.py:hold

chunk_findings.detail: The subprocess child config is `c = NS(ci=NS(max_concurrent_suites=1, suite_wait_s=600))`, but `SL.hold` also reads `suite_queue_stale_s` and `suite_queue_grace_s` (all other tests in this file pass them through `cfg()`/`stale=60`). On this test, the child process exits with `AttributeError` before creating its ticket; `_until(lambda: _tickets(tmp_path) == 1)` then times out and the test fails deterministically.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suitelock_queue.py:test_a_killed_waiter_drops_out_of_the_queue
